FIP.thesis_summary: FTAI Infrastructure (FIP) is the SELLER of Long Ridge Energy & Power to a MARA Holdings subsidiary for ~$1.52B (definitive agreement Apr 29-30, 2026). The resolving event is FERC Section 203 authorization in docket EC26-92-000 (joint application filed May 8, 2026; comments closed May 29, 2026 with a PJM IMM request to condition; no Commission order as of July 17, 2026). Management guided approval to mid-Q3 2026 with FERC the only material condition (HSR/STB customary; no buyer financing condition; $75M reverse break fee; buyer bondholder change-of-control consents already secured May 14-15, 2026; outside date Nov 30, 2026, extendable up to 7 months). Catalyst is real, forward-dated, unfired, and idiosyncratic (resolves on FERC ruling, not the tape). CRITICAL VALUATION FACT: because FIP is the seller, closing delivers ~$1.16B Long Ridge debt elimination, ~$300M parent-level debt repayment and ~$30M/yr interest relief — deleveraging, NOT a per-share consideration to common. The board's $9 target is an undated analyst sum-of-the-parts on the RESIDUAL company (Transtar rail, Jefferson, Repauno), which sits behind ~$1.59B of redemption-value preferred (Series A RailCo ~$1.4B + Series B ~$192M) on negative common equity — it is a second, unforced, undated re-rate, not event-resolved value.
FIP.kill_risk: Even a clean FERC approval and close does NOT deliver the $9: closing pays down parent debt (~$300M) and saves ~$30M/yr interest, but the residual common is a levered stub standing behind ~$1.59B of redemption-value preferred (Series A RailCo redeemable at ~$1,417.49/sh = ~$1.4B, mandatorily redeemable on a rail-business sale, accreting ~$108-129M/yr in kind — outrunning the $30M/yr saved) on total equity of NEGATIVE ~$303M (Q1 2026 10-Q, period 3/31/26), $37.9M unrestricted cash, $3.84B total debt. The $9 SoP requires a second undated re-rate the catalyst itself does not force. Worse, the same 10-Q states the going-concern liquidity plan is alleviated BY the Long Ridge sale — so a deal break does not produce a bounded loss, it removes the stated liquidity plan; downside is undefined, not floored at $3.90 (floor and catalyst are the same object → negatively correlated). The event verifies; the valuation axes the board used do not.

EYPT.thesis_summary: DURAVYU (vorolanib insert) Phase 3 wet-AMD topline — LUGANO (NCT06668064) — is a real, unfired, idiosyncratic binary readout: average change in BCVA at weeks 52/56 vs on-label aflibercept, non-inferiority design, ~400 pts, resolving on its own trial data (not the tape). Guided "beginning mid-2026," registry primary completion Aug-2026, so realistic topline window is Aug–Oct 2026 with twin LUCIA (NCT06682?/NCT06683742) to follow. Win price ~$37.50 (supported by $33 median analyst target) vs a cash-anchored downside ~$3.00. Honest win probability is ~0.42, NOT the board's 0.60: the bull's central "strictly more favorable Phase 3" anchor is false — LUGANO enrolls both treatment-naive and previously-treated eyes, whereas the enabling Phase 2 (DAVIO-2) was previously-treated ONLY, so DURAVYU has zero Phase 2 non-inferiority evidence in the naive, higher-VEGF-burden segment — the exact population where Kodiak's KSI-301 missed NI in DAZZLE.
EYPT.kill_risk: The population-expansion problem may not just shave win-prob — it can push true success toward the market-implied ~0.30–0.35, at which point edge collapses to noise: at p=0.35, EV = 0.35x37.5 + 0.65x3.0 = $15.08 vs a ~$14.2 tape (~6%), on an UNFLOORED overnight-gap binary (loss ~-79%, no stop can catch it). Two live negatives compound the population risk: (1) DURAVYU itself MISSED its Phase 2 primary endpoint in the PAVIA NPDR trial (topline May-2024) — the drug's record is not clean; (2) per the Q1-2026 10-Q (skeptic-cited Note 8; I could not independently re-verify — SEC EDGAR 403'd and the 8-K carried no ATM detail), management drew ~$5.7M on its live ATM at ~$14.75 in Apr–May 2026, i.e. sold equity into its own binary. Modest raise vs $223M cash, but it inverts the bull's "no dilution ahead of print" tell.

DDL.thesis_summary: DDL (Dingdong Cayman) is selling its entire China business to Two Hearts Investments (wholly-owned Meituan subsidiary) for $717M cash under a definitive SPA signed 5 Feb 2026. Shareholders approved on 27 Mar 2026, including authority to apply at least 90% of post-closing cash to buybacks/dividends. No financing condition; the sole open gate is China SAMR anti-monopoly clearance. The event resolves to a capital-return distribution of net cash (retained >=$150M plus up to $280M pre-close sweep plus consideration), well above the current $2.27. Deal binding via no-shop, punitive reverse break fees ($150M/$75M), and a 5 Feb 2027 outside date. Unfired as of 20 Jul 2026 — no filing or clearance announcement since 22 May 2026.
DDL.kill_risk: SAMR can block or condition the sale (China has blocked/conditioned tech deals since 2021); a genuine block breaks the thesis and plausibly prints toward or below the $1.65 52-week low — the market already proved it will NOT capitalize the "net cash floor" on mere regulatory drift, trading to $1.86 (25 Jun 2026) with every floor ingredient public and no block. Secondary: capital return is authorized (90% of post-close cash), not contractually owed — a founder-controlled Cayman board holds discretion, and the retained overseas stub is burning cash (~RMB70M/qtr, up ~242% YoY), so even a clean close leaves per-share distribution dependent on board execution.

The live pending event is deal close itself, guided Q4 CY2026 (special-meeting date still blank in the July 2, 2026 S-4; Outside Date 2027-03-31, extendable to 2027-06-30 for regulatory only). HSR antitrust was already cleared via early termination 2026-03-26; remaining gates are the Gentherm shareholder vote (Share Issuance + Charter Amendment), the IRS private-letter ruling, and consummation of the Separation/Distribution with SpinCo financing (Gentherm's own $550M revolver was refinanced 2026-06-29).
